schemaVersion.description: Config format version. Always 2 for this file. A legacy schemaVersion 1 .claude/project.json (old delegation.devModel/reviewModel/prReviewModel keys) is still read and normalized on load, with a deprecation warning; init-config.sh converts it to this v2 project.yaml shape.

project.description: Identity of the repo this config governs: its name, main branch, and branch-naming convention.

name.description: Project identity, in <org-or-user>/<repository> form matching the repo's real GitHub coordinates (e.g. Zugruul/development-skills) — not a bare short name. Used to qualify feedback-feed refs across a multi-project archive (<project.name>#N) and shown in status/summary output. For a shorter human-facing label, set displayName instead.

displayName.description: Optional human-facing label for this repo, shown in place of the checkout's folder name in the neural-view HUD (repo regions, tooltips, boards panel, brain sidebar). Use when the folder name differs from how the project is actually known (e.g. an npm scope or product name). Purely cosmetic — `name` and the repo's discovery key are unaffected.

description.description: Free-text one-line summary of the project, shown in setup/status output. Optional.

mainBranch.description: The branch tasks merge into (e.g. main, master). Used by gate.sh, board.sh, and the merge/sync protocols as the diff/merge base.

branchPattern.description: Branch name template. Placeholders: <prefix> (spec taskPrefix, lowercased), <id> (task number, zero-padded as issued), <slug> (kebab-case title).

boards.description: GitHub Projects this config drives (usually one; a monorepo may declare several). specs[].board and delegation route to a board by its `id`. The first entry is the default board.

id.description: Local identifier; specs reference boards by this id. First board is the default.

provider.description: Board backend. Only 'github-project' (a GitHub Projects v2 board, driven via `gh project`/`gh api` through board.sh) is supported today.

repo.description: owner/name of the repo where issues live.

projectNumber.description: The Project's number as shown in its GitHub URL (…/projects/<N>).

projectId.description: GraphQL node id (PVT_...). Discover with: board.sh fields

fields.description: GraphQL field/option ids for this board's single-select fields, so board.sh can mutate items without re-discovering ids on every call. Discover with `board.sh fields`.

priority.description: Option key order in `options` = priority order, highest first.

estimate.description: Optional numeric estimate field (e.g. story points/hours), used by telemetry.py's estimate-vs-actual report.

fieldId.description: GraphQL node id of the estimate number field.

statusFlow.description: Ordered pipeline, e.g. [Backlog, In progress, In review, QA, Ready, Deployed]. Names must match status field option keys.

labels.description: Repo labels applied by `board.sh add`/`bug`. `board.sh ensure-labels` idempotently creates any of these missing on the repo (also run by setup-project / seed-board.sh).

bug.description: Label applied by `board.sh bug` (alias of `add --type bug`). Default: type:bug.

feature.description: Label applied by `board.sh add --type feature`. Default: type:feature.

inbound.description: Label applied by `board.sh add --type inbound` (ad-hoc captures via create-inbound). Default: inbound.

specs.description: The spec document(s) this project's board tasks are drawn from. Usually one; a monorepo may run several specs against the same or different boards.

title.description: Human-readable spec title, shown in status/summary output.

board.description: boards[].id this spec's tasks live on.

specPath.description: Repo-relative path to the spec document.

backlogPath.description: Repo-relative path to the backlog doc with per-task acceptance criteria.

taskPrefix.description: Task id prefix; issue titles look like '<taskPrefix>-<number>: <title>'. Must be unique across specs.

epics.description: Ordered by build sequence. Position in this array is the sequencing rank.

id.description: Epic identifier, referenced by other epics' blockedBy[].epic.

taskRanges.description: Inclusive [lo, hi] task-number ranges belonging to this epic.

blockedBy.description: Epic-level dependency guards: this epic's tasks are not picked by next.py until every named epic reaches its untilStatus.

epic.description: Epic id (same spec) that must complete first.

untilStatus.description: Every task of that epic must have reached this status (or later in statusFlow).

invariants.description: Hard rules agents must never violate (fed into implementation briefs verbatim).

work.description: PR-less local delivery + board-sync batching policy (SW-079) + checkout placement (#532). Absent == { type: pr, checkout: worktree } (today's default: push a branch, open a GitHub PR, review + merge via gh; each task's work happens in its own git worktree, registered up front via a draft PR).

checkout.description: WHERE a task's work happens (#532) — delivery-agnostic (valid under type: pr and local alike; work.type governs HOW work lands, this governs WHERE it is written). worktree (default, preferred): each task gets its own git worktree + branch, registered BEFORE implementation (empty registration commit, push, draft PR). main: no branch — work lands directly on project.mainBranch; with methodology.maxInProgress > 1 the orchestrator serializes workers' edits and requires complete small commits as the work goes. The build-next/implement-task skills ask which to use once per session (worktree recommended); the in-session answer wins over this recorded preference.
enumDescriptions: Each task in its own git worktree + branch; the work is registered up front — branch pushed and draft PR opened (even effectively empty) BEFORE implementation starts.
No branch — commits land directly on project.mainBranch; concurrent workers are serialized by the orchestrator (one worker's uncommitted changes at a time, complete small commits as they go).

type.description: How a task's work is delivered. pr (default): push the branch, open a GitHub PR, review it, `gh pr merge`. local: the branch stays local — review is `git diff <main>..<branch>`, approval is recorded as an ISSUE comment, and the orchestrator squash-merges locally (role attribution in the commit) and pushes main (skipped, with a stated reason, if the repo has no remote).
enumDescriptions: Push the branch, open a GitHub PR, review + merge it via gh (today's default).
No PR is ever opened — review the local diff, record approval as an issue comment, and squash-merge locally.

sync.description: Only valid when type: local — governs WHEN queued board mutations flush. Rejected (validate-config.py) when type is pr, since PR delivery already syncs the board in real time as a side effect of each step.

mode.description: Board-sync cadence for local delivery. In every mode, a `blocked` or `new-item` event ALWAYS syncs immediately (the safety valve) — never held back for batching. See scripts/work-mode.sh should-sync.
enumDescriptions: Every board transition syncs immediately, same as PR delivery.
Board mutations batch via the board queue and flush when a task closes.
Board mutations batch and flush at iteration/session boundaries.
Board mutations only flush via an explicit board.sh flush call.

commit.description: Commit-message conventions (#418): how agents write commit subjects, PR titles, and squash-merge subjects/bodies. Motivated by the generated CHANGELOG (#404) rendering a squash body verbatim -- dense prose there is unreadable to a human, so commit language is a product surface, not just an agent-prose habit. Absent == { convention: conventional-commits } plus the documented default systemPrompt below -- additive-only, consumed only as prose by implement-task's dev-brief template and build-next/references/auto-review.md's squash-merge step (no runtime code reads this section today).

convention.description: Which commit-message convention this repo's commit subjects/PR titles/squash-merge subjects follow. Any non-empty string is accepted (a custom in-house convention validates as free text), but these presets are recognized and documented: 'conventional-commits' (default) -- https://www.conventionalcommits.org, `type(scope): description`; 'angular' -- the stricter, fixed type/scope Angular convention conventional-commits itself descends from, with a strict subject length limit; 'gitmoji' -- an emoji prefixes (or replaces) the type word, e.g. `:bug: fix the widget cache`; 'plain' -- Tim Pope's 50/72 style, a short imperative summary line with no type prefix at all. An empty string is invalid.

systemPrompt.description: Free-text instruction injected at the preparing-to-commit phase to control commit-message LANGUAGE/STRUCTURE (the body's prose, distinct from `convention` above which governs the subject line's shape). Absent == "Simple titles. Enumerated bullet-point lists of the changes. Simple human language." When present, must be non-empty.

docs.description: Documentation sets the reviewer enforces: when a diff touches files under a set's `covers` globs and changes behavior/contracts/usage, that set's docs must be updated in the same PR (or the PR must state why not). Standalone repo: one entry covering everything. Monorepo: one entry per package/app plus an optional root entry.

path.description: Repo-relative docs location — a directory (docs/) or a file (README.md).

covers.description: Code-path globs this doc set documents. A diff touching a covered path puts this set in review scope.

notes.description: What belongs in this doc set (helps the reviewer judge 'needed a doc update' vs not).

commands.description: Project-specific shell commands the workflow's scripts shell out to (gate.sh, dev-up skill, etc).

gate.description: Single command that must be green before a task advances to review.

gateFast.description: Optional fast inner-loop test command template.

devUp.description: Command that brings up the full local dev stack.

test.description: Optional standalone test command, when it differs from commands.gate (e.g. gate also lints/typechecks). Not read by any script today; documents intent for humans and future tooling.

delegation.description: Who codes/reviews/orchestrates, as whom, and on which ALLOWED models. In schemaVersion 2 models live INSIDE each identity (there is no delegation.devModel/reviewModel/prReviewModel — those legacy v1 keys are mapped into identities.<role>.models on load).

reviewerTokenEnv.description: Name of an env var holding a GitHub token for a SECOND account (machine user / bot). When set, the auto-merge approval is submitted with that token (GH_TOKEN=$<var> gh pr review --approve), so the PR shows a real distinct approver — GitHub rejects self-approval from the account that opened the PR. When absent, the verdict is posted as a review comment instead.

identities.description: Per-role agent identities (git author + allowed models), ON by default. A role maps to ONE identity or an ARRAY of identities (monorepo routing via `covers`). name/email are templates resolved per-clone by scripts/identity.sh: {name} -> git config user.name, {local}/{domain} -> git config user.email parts — so each person's clone attributes agent commits to their own plus-addressed email. Placeholder-free values are literal (shared bot accounts). Built-in defaults: dev/reviewer/orchestrator names 'Dev Agent - {name}' / 'Reviewer Agent - {name}' / 'Orchestrator Agent - {name}', email {local}+<role>_agent@{domain}; model defaults dev ['claude-sonnet-5'], reviewer ['claude-sonnet-5','claude-sonnet-5[1m]'], orchestrator none. Set a role to null to make it commit as the human; set identities to false to disable all roles.

oneOf.description: Per-role identity overrides. Any key beyond dev/reviewer/orchestrator (additionalProperties) is a custom role name, resolved the same way (identity.sh <role>).

paths.description: Repo-relative locations the workflow's skills/scripts read or write, all optional with sane defaults.

handoffDir.description: Where the handoff skill writes <YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>.md session handoffs. Default: docs/handoffs.

checkpointFile.description: Flag file the build loop checks at the start of every iteration; if present, the loop writes a handoff and stops instead of starting new work. Default: .claude/CHECKPOINT.

designDir.description: Per-epic design docs (<spec-id>-<epic-id>.md) that dev briefs ground on.

specDeltaDir.description: Per-task spec-delta files, folded into the canonical spec when the task's PR merges; applied/ holds history.

devDoc.description: Repo-relative doc with project-specific dev-stack details (ports, profiles, isolation).

methodology.description: Process knobs governing how the build loop works: TDD strictness, concurrency, graduation, UI delegation, and merge/feedback policy.

tdd.description: When true (default), every task is implemented red-first: a failing test commit precedes the implementation commit. Enforced by process/review, not a script gate.

isolationSuite.description: Test path glob for the merge-gating isolation suite, if any (e.g. tests/isolation/**).

maxInProgress.description: Maximum number of tasks worked CONCURRENTLY — THE concurrency knob. It is both the board WIP limit (enforced by next.py's picker) AND the number of parallel implementation lanes. 1 (default) = strictly sequential, one task at a time (the current behavior). N>1 = up to N tasks in parallel, each in its own git worktree + branch + dev agent — only safe for NON-overlapping tasks (see skills/build-next/references/concurrency.md). Set via the concurrency skill / concurrency.sh.

graduationThreshold.description: Note strength (SPEC §8.3) at/above which brain.py graduate-check surfaces a note as a graduation candidate (proposed destination: ROLE.md rule / specs[].invariants entry / test-or-lint). graduate-check is read-only — it proposes; graduation itself stays a human-visible retro action (brain.py graduate).

outcomeWindow.description: Number of most-recent retros (SPEC-GRAPHIFY §7 R7.4/R7.5), counted on the retros.log clock rather than wall time, whose recorded outcomes (brain.py outcome) feed recall's seed-activation multiplier and the ⚠ contested marker. Fewer than N retros ever marked means no window boundary exists yet, so the whole outcome history counts as within-window.

outcomeMultiplierStep.description: Per-net-outcome-point adjustment (SPEC-GRAPHIFY §7 R7.4) applied to a note's seed activation in brain.py recall: multiplier = 1.0 + step × (usefulCount − deadEndCount − correctedCount) within the outcomeWindow, floored at 0.1. A note with zero recorded outcomes, or a net-zero tally, gets EXACTLY 1.0 — byte-identical ranking to a brain with no outcomes.jsonl (G6).

outcomeDeadEndPruneThreshold.description: SPEC-GRAPHIFY §7 R7.6 (GL-004): the minimum FULL-HISTORY (not the outcomeWindow retro window) count of dead_end outcomes, with zero useful outcomes, at which brain.py prune flags a note as a candidate under the outcome rule (reason string names the rule and the count/threshold). Recording a single useful outcome for that note clears the candidacy. Propose-only like every other prune rule — prune --apply never removes note files under this rule, only the pre-existing link-level candidates.

shrinkGuardFraction.description: SPEC-GRAPHIFY §13 shrink guard (lesson from graphify #2053/#2056/#2012): the fraction of a brain's notes/links a single brain.py invocation may remove before it must refuse without --force. Every destructive verb routes through the shared _shrink_guard helper (currently wired into `prune --apply`, its link removal path). The guard only engages when the removal ALSO exceeds an absolute floor (5 items, a code constant) — so e.g. pruning 2 of 3 links in a tiny brain never needs --force. Over threshold without --force: refuses non-zero, prints counts + a sample of the keys that would be removed, writes nothing. Over threshold with --force: proceeds and prints a loud removal summary; LinkPruned events are still emitted either way removal happens.

recencyDecayGraceRetros.description: GL-010: number of retros (retros.log clock, NOT wall time) a note may go untouched before brain.py recall's seed activation starts decaying it. 'Touched' = frontmatter last-touched/created, a links.json per-link `last`, or a recorded `useful` outcome for the note. 0 means decay begins after the very first retro the note goes untouched.

recencyDecayFactor.description: GL-010: multiplicative decay applied per retro elapsed beyond recencyDecayGraceRetros to a note's seed activation in brain.py recall (composes with strength and the outcome multiplier, GL-003). Must be in (0, 1]; 1.0 disables decay entirely.

iterativeUI.description: When true (default), UI-affecting decisions are delegated to the human via the ui-options skill; a local .claude/ITERATIVE_UI_OFF flag also disables it per-clone.

autoMerge.description: When true, build-next skips human PR approval: an autonomous reviewer agent (a suitable model from delegation.identities.reviewer.models) reviews the PR, dialogues fixes with the orchestrator until it approves, then the orchestrator merges and announces the merge. Protocol: build-next skill, references/auto-review.md.

serialDelivery.description: When true, combines with maxInProgress into ONE coherent mode (#423): a task occupies a COUNT-based slot from PICK until MERGE — both In progress AND In review count toward maxInProgress, with no slot ids and no side-car state file (the board is the sole state). next.py's picker allows a NEW pick while occupied (In progress + In review) < maxInProgress -- so maxInProgress: N>1 gives N genuinely parallel implementation lanes -- but once every slot is occupied, an In-progress task is always the actionable next step (RESUME), and only when EVERY occupying task is In review (nothing left to resume) does it print WAIT so the loop can run the merge dance: merges themselves still serialize strictly ONE at a time, FIFO by In-review entry (oldest first), via a merge-dance lock (protocol: build-next/references/concurrency.md). At maxInProgress: 1 this collapses to the original #272 rule (no NEW task while anything else occupies the single slot). Defense in depth: guard-board-move.sh blocks a manual `board.sh move <n> "In progress"` the same way — override with SERIAL_DELIVERY_OVERRIDE=1. Defaults to true for newly generated projects (setup-project/init-config's template) since it is what keeps main honest as maxInProgress grows past 1; an existing repo's explicit value is never overridden by sync-project-configs. Motivated by issue #272 (a 5-deep PR stack that required per-child rebases and lost one PR when GitHub deleted its unmerged base branch) and #423 (parallel lanes needed serialized merges to stop landing under each other).

mergeMethod.description: gh pr merge strategy used by auto-merge — a per-repo decision made at setup. squash (default): linear history; per-role attribution carried as Co-authored-by trailers in the squash body + the PR's own commits. merge: preserves individual role-attributed commits on main. rebase: replays them.
enumDescriptions: Linear history; per-role attribution carried as Co-authored-by trailers in the squash commit body plus the PR link (default).
Keeps the individual role-attributed commits on main as-is.
Replays the branch's commits onto main, preserving them without a merge commit.

feedback.description: Structured per-iteration process feedback about the WORKFLOW (not the project being built), routed at retro time into backlog/brain-note/graduate/upstream/ignore. `true` is shorthand for the defaults shown below. Absent = disabled. Protocol: feedback skill; mechanics: scripts/feedback.py.

enabled.description: Whether feedback collection is on. Redundant with the `true` shorthand — set false here (inside the expanded form) to disable while keeping feed/roles/autoTriage overrides on file for later.

feed.description: Repo-relative path to the yaml feed file (sequence of --- separated loop-feedback records). Default: .claude/feedbacks/feed.yaml — a tracked, orchestrator-mediated archive (committed alongside code, never read/written by dev/reviewer subagents). The legacy, gitignored .claude/feedback/feed.yaml (singular) path is detected and blocks with a migration message when this default is in effect; an explicit override here is trusted as-is.

roles.description: Which identities are expected to emit feedback.

autoTriage.description: When true, triage routes items (e.g. backlog) without a human check-in — mirrors autoMerge's explicit-consent pattern.

entityKinds.description: Cross-identity correlation layer (#163): kind -> home-role map (e.g. {card: card-vault}) used by `brain.py entity-index` and neural-view's live entity-edge derivation to resolve an entity's ANCHOR note -- the note in its kind's home role, when that role has exactly one note declaring the entity. Absent or a kind missing from this map just means entities of that kind always get anchor: null (still correlated, just without a canonical hub); this never affects per-role recall/query.

neuralView.description: Visualization-only knobs for the neural-view HUD. Absent == today's defaults exactly (additive-only); nothing here affects recall, minting, or any brain-mutating command.

entityEdgeColor.description: How neural-view colors cross-role entity-correlation edges (#163): the literal "gradient" (default, also used when this key or the whole neuralView section is absent) blends the two endpoint notes' own brain colors along the edge (vertexColors, source end -> source brain's color, target end -> target brain's color); any other value is treated as a CSS color string and forces every entity edge in this repo to that flat color instead.

compute.description: Remote compute resources AVAILABLE to this project, written by the remote-compute skill (docs/design/remote-compute-plan.md). Normally lives in the gitignored machine-local overlay .claude/project.local.yaml (config.py merges its compute key over the committed config; missing overlay = no compute), because which machines a clone can reach is a property of the machine, not the repo. Capability-style and non-exclusive — the same machine may be enabled in many projects (mirrors assistant.capabilities.<name>); the machine-local cooperative lock serializes actual use, never this declaration. Entries carry only the ssh alias plus an informational capability snapshot — never host, user, or secrets (resolution goes through ~/.ssh/config and the machine-local registry ~/.remote-compute/resources.yaml, which is never committed). Snapshots are documentation: consumers re-probe before real dispatch. Absent == no machines advertised (additive-only).

resources.description: Map keyed by ssh alias (== registry nickname), one entry per machine advertised to this project. Re-enabling the same alias replaces its entry in place; disable keeps the entry with enabled: false, like a disabled capability.

additionalProperties.description: One advertised compute resource: whether it is enabled here, its free-form roles, when its live probe ran, and the capability snapshot taken at that probe.

enabled.description: Whether this project currently treats the resource as available. disable flips this to false without dropping the entry (capability-style).

probedAt.description: UTC ISO-8601 timestamp of the live probe that produced the snapshot (enable never writes from a stale snapshot).

items.description: A free-form role name, e.g. training or inference.

roles.description: Free-form roles tasks may reference instead of the alias (e.g. resource-by-role: training).

capabilities.description: Informational snapshot from the live probe (gpu, ramGB, disks, verified envs). Never authoritative — consumers re-probe before real dispatch.

assistant.description: AST-002 (SPEC-ASSISTANT.md §6): the persistent, LLM-agnostic assistant this repo hosts. Absent == no assistant (additive-only; every other key in this schema validates identically with or without this section). Per §6.1 this section is the SOLE authority for assistant identity/enabled state — the `.neural-network` discovery marker carries no assistant flags. Structure is validated by scripts/assistant/config.py's validate_assistant(); it never resolves binaries/auth (that's AST-006 preflight) and never allowlists `llm.model` (passed verbatim to the adapter).

version.description: Schema version of this assistant: section. Always 1 today.

enabled.description: Whether this assistant is currently offered by discovery/selection. A structurally-valid section with enabled: false still validates — disabling never bypasses the other checks below.

names.description: Non-empty display names for the assistant. The FIRST entry is the main name (used in prompts/UI headers); any remaining entries are aliases it also answers to. Every entry must be a non-empty string.

systemPrompt.description: The assistant's persona, verbatim. names + the identity-brain roster are appended mechanically at turn time — this key holds only the human-authored persona text.

llm.description: Which model backend serves this assistant's turns.

enumDescriptions: Routes through the codex adapter — requires capabilities.codex.enabled: true (§6.5).
Routes through the claude-code adapter — requires capabilities.claude-code.enabled: true (§6.5).
provider.description: Which adapter serves this assistant's turns. Cross-checked against `capabilities` below (§6.5): each provider requires its matching capability enabled, or validate-config.py rejects the section.

model.description: Model id, passed VERBATIM to the adapter (§6.5) — never allowlisted here, since adapters version their own model catalogs independently of this schema.

capabilities.description: Which provider-CLI capabilities are available to this assistant, keyed by capability name (e.g. codex, claude-code). §6.5's provider/capability consistency check reads this map: llm.provider: openai requires capabilities.codex.enabled: true; llm.provider: claude requires capabilities.claude-code.enabled: true.

enabled.description: Whether this capability is available for the assistant to use.

provisioning.description: Capability-specific provisioning hints (e.g. { bin: codex }). Structure is opaque to schema validation — binary/auth resolution is AST-006 preflight, not this schema.

observability.description: Metrics/traces knobs for this assistant's engine (§10.3-§10.5). Absent == observability off.

metrics.description: Metrics-exposition backends, keyed by backend name (e.g. prometheus).

traces.description: Trace-retention backends, keyed by backend name (e.g. sqlite).

assistantObservabilityBackend.description: One assistant observability backend (a metrics or traces exporter, e.g. prometheus or sqlite). retainDays/maxMB are retention knobs (§10.3): age AND size limits, checked independently — 0 means unlimited for that dimension; defaults 30 days / 500MB.

retainDays.description: Retain data for at most this many days. 0 = unlimited (no age-based eviction).

maxMB.description: Retain at most this many megabytes of data. 0 = unlimited (no size-based eviction).

host.description: Bind host for an exposition endpoint (e.g. prometheus). Localhost-only per the assistant's networking invariant.

port.description: Bind port for an exposition endpoint (e.g. prometheus).

roleIdentity.description: How ONE role (dev/reviewer/orchestrator/custom) commits: null (opt out — commits as the human), a single identity, or an array of identities routed by `covers` globs for monorepo per-package agents.

oneOf.description: Opt this role out — it commits as the human.

Several identities for one role (e.g. per-package dev agents). Selection: `covers` globs are matched against the task's changed/expected paths (deterministic, resolved by identity.sh), then the orchestrator judges among ties/no-match. Fallback = the first entry without `covers`, else the first entry.

identity.description: One git-author identity for a role: name/email templates plus its allowed models and (optionally) which paths route to it.

name.description: Template or literal; {name} = git config user.name. Omit to keep the role's default.

email.description: Template or literal; {local}/{domain} = git config user.email parts. Omit to keep the role's default.

models.description: The ONLY models this identity may run on. Either the legacy flat array form (FULL nomenclature ids only, e.g. 'claude-sonnet-5[1m]', 'claude-sonnet-5', 'claude-haiku-4-5', never shorthand like 'sonnet') — the orchestrator picks the most SUITABLE allowed model per task (cheaper/smaller for simple changes, larger-context [1m] for big diffs), never 'always the most powerful'; the reviewer identity's models serve BOTH the two-pass implement-task review AND the auto-merge PR gate — or an object form `{claude: [...], codex: {capability: ...}}` that additionally declares a Codex capability tier (`fast`|`balanced`|`deep-review`|`large-context`), read only by the Codex adapter and never required — omitting `codex` (or using the flat array form) never changes Claude behavior. Omit `models` entirely to use the role's default set.

claude.description: Same FULL-nomenclature Claude model-id list as the flat array form (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-5[1m]', 'claude-sonnet-5'), just nested under this key so `codex` can sit alongside it.

codex.description: Codex-adapter-only settings for this identity; ignored entirely by Claude.

enumDescriptions: Stronger reasoning tier for deep or high-stakes review.
Large-context tier for big diffs or large codebases.
capability.description: Which Codex capability tier this identity may run on.

covers.description: Optional path globs (fnmatch, ** crosses directories). When a task's changed/expected paths match, this identity is selected (monorepo per-package routing). An entry with no `covers` is the fallback.

color.description: Optional hex color for this role's brain in the neural view — nodes, synapses, cluster labels and gauges all derive from its hue. Omit to use the viewer's default palette (dev #ffd24d, reviewer #ff5b7f, orchestrator #38fad4).

singleSelectField.description: A GitHub Projects v2 single-select field: its GraphQL field id plus its option name -> option id map. Used for boards[].fields.status/priority.

fieldId.description: GraphQL node id of the single-select field (PVTSSF_...). Discover with: board.sh fields

options.description: Option name -> option id. Key order is meaningful (statusFlow order / priority order).
